summary: Deploy the new version with a state-only Django migration so the column is untouched by the new code. The old version continues serving traffic and writing customer notes. After the old version is retired, drop the `note` column from `account_user` in a contract SQL stage. This sequence ensures zero downtime, data consistency during overlap, and clean schema removal after the old code is gone.
write_consistency: During the overlap between deploy_new and retire_old, both versions share the same database. The old version includes `note` in all INSERT/UPDATE statements via Django's save(), while the new version's model has the field removed, so its writes omit `note` and it receives the column's database DEFAULT (or NULL). No SQL stages modify the `note` column during overlap, so every customer's `note` remains its most recent value written by either version. After retire_old, the old version is gone, and the contract SQL stage removes the column, after which the runner's consistency check no longer applies.

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version. After this stage, only the new version serves traffic.
Remove the note column from account_user now that the old version is retired and no code references it.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
